title: Why These Four Biotechs Can Afford Not to Sell
summary: argenx, Insmed, Incyte, and Revolution Medicines show why biotech independence depends on product evidence, cash generation, a second growth curve, global execution, and financing without surrendering control.
source_status: Published publicly on Facebook; this complete English edition preserves the argument sequence, company cases, risk hierarchy, figures, references and disclaimer
cover_image_alt: Five capabilities that allow a biotech to remain independent
homepage_cover_image_alt: What it takes for a biotech to decline a sale
core_judgments: Biotech independence is not a posture toward M&A; it is the ability to retain core rights and reinvest one success into another.
A second growth curve determines how long independence can last, while global execution, cash flow, and financing determine whether scientific value reaches the market.
Royalties, convertibles, and loans can preserve control, but they dilute equity, add interest expense, or carve away future cash flow.
